Risk_Description: Because periodic access reviews are not consistently performed, terminated or role-changed employees could retain inappropriate system access, resulting in unauthorized access to sensitive data or fraud.
Existing_Controls: Quarterly access review by IT Manager; access requests require manager approval before provisioning

Risk_Description: Because developers have standing write access to the main production branch, an unauthorized or untested code change could be deployed without review, resulting in system errors or a security vulnerability in production.
Existing_Controls: Branch protection rules requiring 1 peer approval; CI pipeline runs automated tests before merge

Risk_Description: Because the database is not encrypted at rest, a compromised backup or storage volume could expose customer personal data, resulting in a data breach and regulatory notification obligations under GDPR.
Existing_Controls: Network-level access restricted via security groups; VPN required for admin access

Risk_Description: Because the same Finance Operations Specialist can both create new vendor records and approve vendor payments, a fraudulent vendor could be created and paid without independent detection.
Existing_Controls: Monthly reconciliation of vendor master file changes reviewed by Controller (compensating control)

Risk_Description: Because not all company laptops have endpoint detection and response (EDR) software installed, a compromised device could go undetected, resulting in malware spread or data exfiltration.
Existing_Controls: MDM enrollment required at onboarding; EDR deployed to 85% of fleet

Risk_Description: Because the payroll vendor's most recent SOC 2 Type II report has not been reviewed in over 12 months, the company cannot confirm the vendor's controls over employee PII are still operating effectively.
Existing_Controls: Vendor onboarding included initial SOC 2 report review and signed DPA

Risk_Description: Because backup restoration has not been tested in the last 12 months, a disaster recovery event could reveal that backups are corrupted or incomplete, resulting in extended downtime or permanent data loss.
Existing_Controls: Nightly automated backups configured with 30-day retention

Risk_Description: Because the AWS root account does not have multi-factor authentication enforced, a compromised credential could grant an attacker unrestricted control over all cloud infrastructure.
Existing_Controls: Root account credentials stored in a password vault, not used for daily operations

Risk_Description: Because access to customer PII within the support platform is not logged, unauthorized viewing of customer data by support staff could occur without detection.
Existing_Controls: Role-based access limits which support tiers can view full PII fields

Risk_Description: Because a formal data migration reconciliation has not yet been scheduled, incomplete or inaccurate employee data could be carried into the new HR system without detection before go-live.
Existing_Controls: UAT test plan drafted; business owner sign-off required before go-live per SDLC policy
